title: Working out the Mardi Gras number at the Pepper Pot in Gretna
summary: He had the carnival piece before meeting Erickson; Robert Parker places it at the Pepper Pot in Gretna, which drew 300 to 400 a night.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now, this guy Erickson, he asked you to do a call with him?
No, he didn't ask me. Not him. I was doing that before I met him.
Oh, so you were doing this for the people? Yeah. So you had gotten this together on the bandstand? Yeah. Now, Robert Parker told me, he said you got together at the Pepper Pot.
Yeah, different places that we played at this. Because he said he remembered that you were playing at the Pepper Pot at that time. He was working with me at that time.
Yeah. And that was, Pepper Pot was over in Gretna, right? Yeah. Yeah. That was a pretty heavy club, wasn't it? A pretty popular club.
Well, we was drawing from 300 to 400 people a nightly.
Yeah. Where was it in Gretna? I don't know that side of the river that was.
It was on 7th and Y Street. 7th and what? Y.
Y?
Y. Y. Y. Y. Y. Y. Y.
Like you said Bob Y, Fence Y. Oh, W-I-R-E. Y. 7th and Y. That must have been, you must have just taken, what, did you take the ferry over then in those days?
Yeah, you had to, yeah.
Yeah. What did you take, Jackson Avenue or the-? Yeah.
It was the closest, because once you get out off the Jackson area ferry you walk about seven blocks.
Oh, yeah.
And make a right turn, two blocks you was at the place.
Right. You don't know if it's not still together, is it?
It's still there, but it's been remodeled and all. It don't look the same, you know. Mm-hmm. It looked like a real classical late joint, you know. Oh, really?
Yeah.
All the beauty is gone from-
